claims.title: Shell injection risk from unsanitized URL interpolated into single-quoted curl -d body
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Shell injection risk from unsanitized URL interpolated into single-quoted curl -d body**

The documented recipe tells the agent to literally substitute `<target-url>` into a single-quoted `-d` JSON string. If the target URL contains a single quote, the shell will terminate the quoted argument early and any trailing shell syntax in the URL could execute. This is a plausible attack vector since URLs are often derived from external/user-controlled input during research tasks. Consider instructing the agent to build the JSON body via `jq -n --arg url "$URL" '{url:$url}'` or write the URL to a variable and use `printf`/heredoc to avoid manual string interpolation into shell-quoted JSON.

claims.title: Fixed 120s curl timeout may be shorter than documented queue wait
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Fixed 120s curl timeout may be shorter than documented queue wait**

The doc states requests can queue up to 5 deep with gaps of 20-40s for ebay (up to ~200s of pure queue wait before the request even starts, before counting the page's own load time), yet the curl recipe uses a fixed `-m 120`. This mismatch means legitimate eBay fetches can be aborted by curl before the gateway ever serves them, causing the agent to see a curl timeout and incorrectly treat it as a gateway failure.

claims.title: Credential check doesn't gate the subsequent fetch example
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Credential check doesn't gate the subsequent fetch example**

The new unset-credential guard (`[ -n "$STEALTH_BROWSER_URL" ] ... || echo "not configured"`) is a standalone diagnostic snippet. It doesn't actually control whether the `curl ... /content` command below it runs — an agent reading this documentation could still execute the fetch command even when credentials are unset, since the guard and the fetch are separate code blocks with no explicit conditional linking them. The doc should make clear the agent must check this condition and skip the whole step before attempting the fetch, not just print a diagnostic.

claims.title: Unset-credential check doesn't actually gate the health check/content request
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Unset-credential check doesn't actually gate the health check/content request**

The doc shows the env-var presence check and the curl health check as two separate commands run sequentially (`[ -n "$STEALTH_BROWSER_URL" ] && ... || echo "not configured"` followed by an unconditional `curl ...`). If the variables are unset, the first line just echoes "not configured" and the second line still executes, sending a curl request with an empty URL/Authorization header. The agent following this literally would not actually skip the gateway step on missing credentials, contradicting the stated intent ('If either is unset, skip the gateway and go to the next escalation step'). The two commands should be combined so the health check only runs when credentials are present (e.g., using `&&` to chain into the curl, or an explicit early-return/skip instruction).

claims.title: Credential check result not actually used to gate the fetch
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Credential check result not actually used to gate the fetch**

The health-check snippet prints `200` or `not configured`/error codes to stdout but the doc doesn't show the result being captured into a variable or conditional that controls whether the subsequent 'Fetching a page' curl call runs. An agent executing this literally as two separate shell snippets could run the health check, see non-200 output, and still proceed to the fetch snippet since there's no `if` wrapping it. This mirrors the previously-flagged 'credential-unset check doesn't gate subsequent curl calls' issue and remains unresolved in this diff.

claims.title: Credential-unset check doesn't gate the actual fetch recipe
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Credential-unset check doesn't gate the actual fetch recipe**

The health-check snippet in the Credentials section correctly gates on `STEALTH_BROWSER_URL`/`STEALTH_BROWSER_TOKEN` being set, printing `not configured` and instructing to skip if unset. However, the separate 'Fetching a page' curl recipe below (and the equivalent in SKILL.md) does not itself check these variables before running — it relies on the agent having already performed the health check and remembered the outcome in a separate shell invocation. Since each bash block here is typically executed as an independent command, an agent that skips (or forgets) the health-check step could fire the fetch curl with empty `$STEALTH_BROWSER_URL`/`$STEALTH_BROWSER_TOKEN`, sending a malformed request to a blank URL (e.g. `curl ... -X POST "/content"`) instead of cleanly skipping as intended.

claims.title: Credential check in SKILL.md example is illustrative only and may not actually gate execution
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Credential check in SKILL.md example is illustrative only and may not actually gate execution**

The SKILL.md text says "if either is unset, skip to step 4 without hunting for credentials," but SKILL.md itself no longer shows the actual bash gating logic (it was moved to stealth-browser.md as `if [ -n "$STEALTH_BROWSER_URL" ] && [ -n "$STEALTH_BROWSER_TOKEN" ]; then ... fi`). Since SKILL.md only narrates the behavior rather than encoding it, an agent that doesn't fully read the referenced doc could still issue a curl call with empty env vars. This is a minor documentation-robustness gap (same class as the codex finding from the prior round), not a code defect, so it's low severity for a docs-only PR.
